title: Room for error, "enough"
principle: Plans built on precise, optimistic assumptions break the moment reality deviates from them. Build in margin — savings beyond what feels necessary, spending below what you could technically afford — so ordinary bad luck doesn't turn into a crisis. Knowing what "enough" looks like protects you from the moving goalpost of always wanting more.
formula: Guard thresholds (emergency fund floor, installment cap) exist to keep an automatic margin, not just to react to a single bad month.
fitsWhen: You're deciding how conservative to be about savings targets, debt limits, or any plan that assumes the future will go roughly as expected.
critique: Too much margin has a real cost too — capital sitting idle as a buffer isn't working for you; the right amount of room for error depends on how volatile your actual life and income are, not a universal number.
